purpose: Establish a resolved Info-mode GPU timing baseline for the AMD Quality stack with IBL and Volumetric Shadows enabled in an exterior SteamVR null-HMD scene.

sourceSnapshot.buildConfiguration: VR Release; DEVBENCH_BRIDGE=ON; AUTO_PLUGIN_DEPLOYMENT=OFF; full AIO staged from the source snapshot

dependencies.name: CommonLibSSE-NG
dependencies.notes: Revision and clean state were verified directly in the submodule.

runtimeLane.notes: The game used the vanilla openvr_api.dll with OCU disabled. The SteamVR null driver owned the active HMD. This lane provides no OCU or OpenXR evidence.

hmd.profile: CSX Null HMD Info Baseline; 1512x1680 per eye; 90 Hz; IPD 0.063 m; forcedDriver=null; requireHmd=false

scene.poseScript: SteamVR null-driver fixed HMD pose; no controller input; camera observed at [172837.375, -93980.4453125, 11169.5], yaw 1.68246114
scene.motionProfile: static HMD pose with live exterior scene
controlledVariables: Settled exterior save loaded through DevBench
Screenshot capture remained disabled during the timing pass

issues: Automated stereo capture is unavailable at Info because CSX requires Developer Mode for that mutation; no visual conclusions are attached to this timing-only run.
The explicit ImageBasedLighting timers cover SH projection dispatches, not the IBL work composed into lighting shaders across the scene.
The explicit VolumetricShadows timers cover its downsample and blur compute passes, not every downstream consumption cost.

artifacts.role: Raw resolved CSX profiler responses for 38 unique captured frames
Completed identity record for the branch-matched Info shader cache
Deterministic SHA-256 manifest for all files in the completed Info ShaderCache tree

controlledVariables: One exterior save, weather, and static HMD pose
deviations: No visual pass was run because automated capture is intentionally unavailable at Info.
This is an on-state baseline, not an IBL-off or Volumetric-Shadows-off counterfactual comparison.

reasons: CSX confirmed Info level 2 and successfully loaded IBL 1.1.3 and Volumetric Shadows 2.5.0.
The disk cache completed before the scene and profiler pass; no shader compilation overlapped the samples.
All 38 profiler frames were unique and resolved with zero timer-slot refusals.
The raw profiler artifact, exact settings, runtime lane, scene, hardware, and cache identity are retained.

conclusions: This run is the first reusable Info timing baseline for the AMD Quality stack with IBL and Volumetric Shadows enabled in the recorded Riften lane.
The observed CSX top-level GPU total averaged 5.0943 ms with a 6.0058 ms p95; no Debug comparison is valid because the earlier Debug run used a different scene and settings.
Volumetric Shadows' explicit compute passes averaged 0.0481 ms in this scene.
IBL's explicit SH projection dispatches were usually below timer resolution, but that does not measure its lighting-shader integration cost.
A separately paired Developer-Mode visual pass and on/off counterfactual runs are required before making preset-quality or marginal-cost decisions.
notes: Preparing the first optimized Info cache from the Debug seed took approximately 770 seconds of wall time.

Eleven scene-generated files from MO2 overwrite were hash-verified, merged into the named Info cache after Skyrim exited, and the active overwrite ShaderCache directory was removed to prevent cross-lane contamination.
The completed Info cache contains 3616 ShaderCache files. Its Info.ini SHA-256 is 1B4604FB8AF6C66A06DA9FE213791F30DB03FA2AA769833F5D1CE5F27466680E.
Temporary SteamVR and MO2 configuration changes were restored byte-for-byte after the run.
